reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is a creator-led review and tutorial promoting BTCC as a cryptocurrency exchange, including a signup bonus and referral link. It asks viewers to sign up through that link, create an account, and deposit cryptocurrency to trade, but the tutorial also explains how futures trading works and warns that trading is risky and losses are possible. The promotional claims and referral-linked bonus are concrete, but the video does not establish that the bonus or exchange is deceptive.

opening.argument: Judge the bonus alongside the action requested to obtain it. The description says, “Sign up now,” and promises up to $11,000 in bonuses through its link. The speaker directs viewers to use that link, create an account, and verify an email address. The walkthrough continues to a crypto deposit address and instructs viewers to send USDT there. That sequence makes the reward an inducement to enter a specific signup and funding path, not merely a passing mention of an exchange. “Up to” leaves the amount any particular viewer would receive unresolved; the large headline figure does the persuasive work before its conditions are established.

rebuttal.rebuttal: A trading tutorial and a demo mode do not sever the bonus from the requested signup. The speaker explicitly says the bonus and fee discount apply “when you use my link.” The deposit walkthrough then describes sending crypto to an address. The defense identifies genuine instruction, but that does not answer whether the prominent reward claim is being used to move viewers through the linked account and funding flow.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited sequence shows a promotional signup offer followed by instructions for using an exchange. It does not show that the bonus is unavailable or that the deposit address is fraudulent. The speaker distinguishes practice with virtual funds from trading live funds and later explains withdrawals. An unspecified maximum bonus warrants caution, but these sources do not establish deceptive acquisition.

opening.argument: Consider the signals together: a headline advertising an $11,000 bonus and no KYC or VPN; a description urging immediate signup for “free bonuses”; and a speaker praising leverage of up to 225x while saying the link brings signup bonuses and a fee discount. The pitch combines easy access, a conspicuous reward, and an invitation into highly leveraged trading. The description's separate links advertising daily returns add to the promotional context. None of these elements alone proves deception. Together, they give a careful judge reason to question whether the attractive headline is drawing viewers toward financial risk while leaving the practical value of the bonus unexplained.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the video includes trading instruction and a demo option. Those features do not explain the conditions behind the headline bonus. Nor does a general warning that “Crypto is risky” resolve the tension between that warning and the prominent invitation to sign up for free bonuses. The concern is how these messages work together, not whether every part of the tutorial lacks educational value.

opening.argument: The review format should not obscure what the presentation asks viewers to do. The speaker says they partnered with BTCC, links the partnership to up to $11,000 in signup bonuses, and tells viewers to take advantage of the “free stuff.” The tutorial begins account setup by directing viewers to the description link, then walks through depositing funds. Operational detail can make the path feel familiar and credible, but it also carries viewers from the endorsement to participation. The question is whether this is primarily an independent explanation or a reward-led solicitation dressed in the form of one. The speaker's own partnership disclosure and repeated linked offer support the latter reading.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls this a creator-led tutorial, and the walkthrough is real. But the opening also acknowledges the partnership, referral link, bonus, and deposit instructions. Those are not incidental details: the speaker places the linked account creation at the start of the process. Showing how trading controls work does not make the repeated request to join through the promotional link irrelevant to judging the video's purpose.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The partnership is disclosed rather than concealed, and promotion does not itself make a tutorial deceptive. The speaker spends substantial time explaining order types, leverage, position sizing, stop-losses, and withdrawals. Crucially, the cited offer says “up to” $11,000; the wrong-side argument supplies no evidence that the stated offer is false or that the demonstrated exchange functions are fabricated.
